name: Jorja Smith
milestone_by_age_26: Featured twice on Drake's chart-topping 'More Life' playlist in March 2017 at age 19, after her independently released single 'Blue Lights' went viral and she placed on the BBC Sound of 2017 list.
early_history_summary: Smith began performing at age 8 and writing songs at 11, raised in Walsall by a former musician father and jewellery designer mother. She uploaded YouTube covers as a teen and was discovered by a manager at 15, signing with Sony/ATV at 18 and releasing her breakthrough single 'Blue Lights' while still a teenager.
family_context_summary: Born to a Jamaican father (Peter, a benefits officer and former neo-soul singer) and an English mother (Jolene, a jewellery designer) in Walsall, West Midlands.
parent_family_domain_summary: Her father was the lead singer of neo-soul group 2nd Naicha and encouraged her to take piano lessons at 8 and classical singing; both parents were significant musical influences.

evidence_summary: Jorja Smith grew up in a musical household in Walsall with a father who had been a neo-soul singer and who encouraged her classical and piano training from age 8. She won a music scholarship to Aldridge School, began writing songs at 11, and uploaded YouTube covers that were discovered by a manager at 15. Her independently released single 'Blue Lights' went viral in 2016, leading to her BBC Sound of 2017 placement and two features on Drake's 'More Life' at age 19, which exponentially expanded her audience.
starting_point: Born to a Jamaican former musician father and English jewellery designer mother in Walsall, West Midlands; working-class upbringing with strong musical household.
current_position: Active recording artist; released album 'Falling or Flying' in 2023; BRIT Award winner; resides in London.

parent_family_domain_summary: No documented musical professional background in the family, though Mai grew up idolizing Lauryn Hill, Mary J. Blige, and Alicia Keys and joined her local church choir.

Her third EP 'Ready' contained 'Boo'd Up,' which became a sleeper hit a year after release, reaching #5 on the Hot 100 and winning a Grammy.
